extracted.intended_audience: proofreaders, copyholders, authors, and editors involved in preparing manuscripts for print
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for proofreaders and copyholders working on galley- and page-proofs for book and periodical production, covering conduct, workflow, proofreader's marks, and detailed typographic/style rules. Also an index of the Manual of Style's scope (capitalization, punctuation, italics, hyphenation, numerals, footnotes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all queries in the proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful to answer all queries in the proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays and errors often result from not attending to queries. Queries in the manuscript should be transferred to the proof, or attention should be directed in the manuscript to the proof. In asking questions of authors or editors, make your point clear; a simple query is often not enough to draw attention to the particular point you have in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize post-typesetting changes / cost awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that changes in the type cost money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The omission or addition of a word in the middle of a paragraph may necessitate resetting the whole of this from that point on; and if such alteration is made in the page-proof, it may further involve repaging the entire article or chapter. Make your manuscript as perfect as possible before delivering it to the printer. Any necessary alterations should be made in the galley-proof, as each succeeding stage will add to the cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid corrections in plates
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections in plates should be studiously avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not only are corrections in plates expensive, but they are apt to injure the plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return original manuscript and previous marked sets with proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The original manuscript should in each instance be returned with the galley-proof, and each successive set of proofs returned should be accompanied by the previous marked set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will assist in calculating the cost of alterations properly chargeable to you and allow the proofreader to refer to the original if any question arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read as if you were the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Read everything as if you yourself were the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be particularly careful about proper names and figures; if the copy is not perfectly clear or you doubt its correctness, look it up or query the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be precise and discreet in queries to authors/editors
rubrics_metrics.description: In asking questions of authors or editors, make your point clear and be discreet; do not stultify yourself by asking foolish questions on the proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple query is often not enough. The author will be thankful for sensible suggestions but will resent trivial criticisms. Do not ask authors or editors to decide questions of style—the Manual of Style is primarily meant for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn the Manual of Style; don't ask about style
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ask authors or editors to decide questions of style. The Manual of Style is primarily meant for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn its rules so that you may correct any violation of them you may come upon, without asking questions. Do not waste time over matters of style; the proofreader is supposed to know the rules without your telling him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know individual preferences ('personal equation')
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a study of the 'personal equation' in the case of those individuals (editors and others) with whom you as a proofreader will constantly have to deal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One person may expect of you as a matter of course what another might regard as an unwarranted interference; adapt accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct palpably wrong items even if copy asserts otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Never hesitate to correct anything that is palpably wrong, however positively the copy may assert the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that the blame for the error will eventually be laid at your door, and justly so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not follow copy blindly; you are the judge of correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not follow copy blindly, unreasoningly. Follow copy only when, and as far as, it is correct. Whether or not it is correct, you are the judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excuses like 'I thought the copy was edited' or 'I thought the author knew what he wanted' are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not shirk responsibility because of others' approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fall into the fallacy that the author's or editor's O.K. relieves you of all or any part of your responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors depend on the proofreader to ensure typographical requirements are met and the adopted style adhered to, and they affix signatures on that supposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate disagreements with copyholder; proofreader is arbiter
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not shield yourself behind your copyholder. The copyholder is there to assist you, not to tell you how to do things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you think you have cause to doubt her version of a matter, investigate for yourself. Do not suggest to the copyholder the reading of a word or phrase which she has difficulty in making out from the manuscript; remember you are the arbiter, and not the compositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize accuracy over speed; handle rushes with disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not permit yourself to be stampeded. Cultivate speed, but remember that accuracy is even more important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary time is not given, take it — within reasonable limits — to do things right. In unavoidable cases of 'rush' protect yourself by letting it be understood you have done your best in the time allotted, but that you must disclaim any further responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark ownership of work reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Put your initial at the top of every galley you read or revise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This saves time in tracing proofs and ensures credit where it belongs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyholder voice and enunciation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate a low, soft, clear reading-voice. Only your own proofreader has to hear you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the proofreader's point of view, small words are as essential as big ones: get them all in — and get them in right. Enunciate plural 's' distinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyholder conduct and positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not get offended when your reader asks you to repeat; regulate and equalize your speed; sit at right angles to your reader if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not race through typewritten copy while fumbling manuscript. Sitting at right angles helps you hear the reader and watch his hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't guess words; inspect manuscript closely
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not keep guessing at a word. Look at it closely, consider the context, and do not speak it until you have made it out — or at least made the very best guess possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give your reader a chance to make corrections; slow up the moment he puts his pencil to the paper to avoid redoing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop efficient signaling/code with your reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolve your own system of signals; do not waste time by saying 'in italics' for every word or letter so treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use raised voice, a tap of the pencil for each word, or other private code intelligible only to you and your reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful transferring marks; organize proofs for dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful in transferring marks; a mark in the wrong place means two errors uncorrected in place of one corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In sending out proofs, ensure everything is there: arrange copy and proof-sheets neatly and consecutively. Never send out proofs for the first time without consulting the job ticket for the number wanted and the name and address of the person to whom they are to be sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript/proof accompaniment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should accompany the galley-proof; the foul proof (author's marked galley-proof) should accompany the page-proof; if no galley-proof has been sent, the manuscript should accompany the page-proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this order so reviewers have necessary reference material for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Envelope and physical handling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate in the lower left-hand corner the contents of all the envelopes you address; fasten your pins in the center at the top, not diagonally in the left-hand corner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pins placed diagonally may cover up directions often written in that corner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain proof-room housekeeping and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Return every evening to the file or the bookcase any volume taken out for reference during the day; keep the proof-room neat and orderly and maintain records and files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfect your system so that everything can be located at a moment's notice; the more housekeeping you do without being asked, the more appreciated you will be.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and learn standard proofreader's marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the standard set of proofreader's marks to indicate corrections (capitals, small capitals, lower case, type size changes, delete, indent, insert space, close up, bad spacing — 'vspacemore evenly,' wrong font or size, transpose, carry left/right, indent/make new paragraph, depress, imperfect letter — correct, space shows between words — shove down, straighten crooked line, restore words crossed out, print as a logotype, words omitted, Query to author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn the marks and their meanings so changes are unambiguous; the Manual supplies a list of marks and their standard interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply capitalization rules consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow detailed rules for capitalization: proper nouns, adjectives from proper nouns, names of organizations, titles, geographic names, historical epochs and events, biblical books, legislative/judicial/administrative bodies, academic degrees, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Manual contains extensive entries (e.g., rules for capitalization of administrative bodies, artistic schools, feast-days, titles of works). Consult the appropriate sections (1–57) for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply italics rules appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Use italics for emphasis, titles of books and works, foreign words and phrases, symbols indicating subdivisions, letters representing unknown quantities, names of genera and species, and initial word 'Resolved' in certain contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules and exceptions are collected in the Manual (sections 58–73); know when to italicize vs. roman-quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow hyphenation and compound-word rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the Manual's hyphenization rules for compound adjectives, compounds with prefixes (co-, bi-, non-, re-, etc.), fraction hyphenation, omission of common element indicated by hyphen, list of hyphenated words, and avoidance of unnecessary division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphen rules and hyphenization guidance are found in sections 182–214, including special compounds (father, mother, fellow, maker, life, store, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow punctuation rules (commas, colons, dashes, periods, ellipses, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to rules for comma usage (series, adjectives, appositives, clauses), colon use (introductions, emphases, times), dash usage (breaks, emphasis, parenthetical material, to indicate omission or implication), period placement (quotations, abbreviations, headlines), ellipses, exclamation and interrogation points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules and illustrations are in the Manual (commas 141–62; colon 131–36; dashes 166–75; periods 122–26; ellipses 180–81; exclamation 127–38; interrogation 129–30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for division of words and line-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply systems and rules for division of words (avoid unnecessary division, avoid divisions on certain letters, rules for hyphenation at line breaks), and avoid divided words at end of next-to-last line or bottom of recto page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult sections 215–30 for division rules, systems (221), and use of hyphen to indicate division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals, figures and number formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat numbers according to Manual guidance: when to spell out numbers, when to use figures (round numbers, groups of digits), spacing of Arabic/Roman numerals at paragraph starts, comma usage for thousands, dash for ranges, treatment of percentages and monetary symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rules summarized in sections 94–101, 152–60, and notes on columns of figures and table formatting (244, 344).

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes, references, and citation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Manual's general style for footnotes: numbering, indices for references, exceptions, classical and literary reference styles, use of ibid., loc. cit., op. cit., and abbreviations (e.g., e.g., i.e.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 231–38 and 336–38 address indices for footnotes, how to number, placing, sequence, and samples for various journals and styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and cross-reference conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply indexing rules (italicizing 'See' and 'See also' in cross-references), treatment of prefixes/particles in proper nouns, and general indexing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult indexing section (239) for details and rules for cross-references and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table and leader formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up headings for open tables, use leaders for blanks in columns of figures, use double rules in tables as required, and follow spacing and alignment rules for table heads and columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections on tables and leaders (240–50, 243, 347) for specimen layouts and linotype/monotype considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and typography definitions (galley, page-proof, foul proof, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the definitions and handling of production stages and typographic terms: galley, galley-proof, page-proof, foul proof, foundry-proof, make-up, drop-folio, em/en/quad, hair-space, font, face, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and handling instructions are provided throughout the Manual (glossary-like entries and production notes: galley 285, page-proof 286, foul proof 288, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign words, translations, and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Italicize words and phrases from foreign languages or roman-quote English equivalents as required; treat quoted foreign passages according to rules for quotation and translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections for foreign languages and equivalent English (59, 78, 85) and for how to handle translations and passages quoted from foreign languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized style rules for names, titles, and institutional designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow detailed prescriptions for capitalization, abbreviation, and formatting of names (Christian names, particles like Mc/Mac, titles like Rev./Hon.), institutional names, governmental bodies, degrees, and titles in addresses and signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Manual entries on names, titles, civil/military/administrative bodies, abbreviations, and formatting (see index entries for specific cases: 1–57 for capitals, 21–22 for degrees, 49 for University of Chicago divisions).
